artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: The v0.20 core, on the round-2 build e29adc9fa7. (13) the key is (account, IDENTIFIER) where the identifier is the first non-empty of the declared identifier columns, and `_unident` is carried in BOTH the grouping and the day-t price join so an UNIDENTIFIED row can never be priced by an identifier; (14) an identifier-less row priced 1.00 with quantity == value is cash, every other one is excluded; (15) `in_basket = member & (value >= 0)`, so the denominator is the long holdings plus POSITIVE cash, and `negative_value` + `leveraged` carry what is outside it (cash_value stays SIGNED); (16) a second-pass band on the computed answer emits the fifth status IMPLAUSIBLE-RETURN with a NULL daily_return; (17) unchanged, but the manifest population moved to the new `held_count`. Also: `PartitionCache`, a bounded thread-safe LRU, because every day reads its own positions partition and its prior day's -- measured 226 hits / 1,445 misses over the 557-day 49F run and 634 / 2,590 over the 1,609-day INF run. Run ad hoc from the working tree for QA; no S3 code prefix and no schedule here. Naming gate on the commit diff: PASS, 1 graded, 0 REFUSE. commit-gate (py_compile + ds-precommit + ruff py39) clean.

Declaration schema 1.0 -> 1.1 and the Inflection channel added AS AN ENTRY, never a code branch. New fields, each carrying its measured basis and denominator: `identifier_columns` (ordered, ruling 13), `quantity_column` (ruling 14's cash test), `account_id_zero_pad` (10 for 49F, 0 for INF -- the Orion accountId is a 3-to-5 character integer key and padding it would invent digits), `cash_flag_column` (INF's isCustodialCash) and `monolith`. THE NAMING LIMB REFUSED THE FIRST CUT AND THE REFUSAL WAS CORRECT: an authored JSON carrying the registered token `inflection` is a hand-kept carrier under LGIC_ENFORCE DEC-6 (3 REFUSE lines at sources.json:41, :43, :46). So the entry is keyed `orion`, declares `monolith: orion`, and its positions_prefix is the TEMPLATE `{monolith}/{scope}/silver/fact_positions/`; firm_scope() resolves a monolith to its unique registry scope and REFUSES when the monolith carries any other number -- measured at the cut, orion 1, eclipse 1, blackdiamond 2, so the first Black Diamond channel declared this way stops loudly instead of picking a firm. The token now exists only in infra/logic/registry/.

python -m pytest data/assets/scripts/gold/irpt_holdings_performance/tests/ -q -> 24 passed (was 13). The four the amendment names: two identifier-less positions at different prices stay TWO positions (a merged key reports one, which is the +1e57 mechanism); an identifier-less cash row joins the basket (+0.04 not +0.10) with BOTH near-misses excluded -- quantity != value, and price 1.01; a margin-debit account reads +0.01 where the netted base read +1.00, with leveraged true and the debit visible; the +/-100% band tested AT ITS EDGE (exactly +1.0 is not computable, 0.999 is an ordinary day). Plus the structural claim that a long-only basket cannot reach -100% (a 100.00 -> 0.01 collapse stays OK at -0.9999), four Inflection cases, a short-only account's place in the completeness population, and the no-cash-carrier refusal. TWO EXISTING TESTS CHANGED AND BOTH CHANGES ARE THE RULING: `test_the_status_vocabulary_is_closed` counts five members instead of four (ruling 16 is an emission-contract change and this count is where it is recorded), and the NON-POSITIVE-BASE fixture moved from a cash debit to a short-only book, because under ruling 15 a debit no longer reaches that member -- which is the defect being retired, not a weakened check. No 49F METHOD test was altered.

mutant.description: TWO planted mutants, one per claim, each written through the SAME parquet path the producer writes so it is indistinguishable from a real bad emission, and each RESTORED by re-running the producer for that day rather than by writing the good bytes back. M1 attacks ruling 16's claim: one OK row in the landed 49F date=2026-09-25 daily partition (account 0010023253) was given daily_return = 1.5. M2 attacks the INF completeness claim: account 100 was dropped from the landed INF date=2026-09-25 daily partition, 960 rows to 959.
mutant.expected: M1 -> E3-AC4 FAIL naming 1 OK row at |r| >= 1, then PASS at 0 after the restore. M2 -> E3-AC1 FAIL naming 1 missing account, then PASS at 0 after the restore.
mutant.observed: M1 PLANTED: 'OK rows |r|>=1: 1 | OK rows |r|>0.5: 5' / E3-AC4 FAIL. M1 RESTORED: 'OK rows |r|>=1: 0 | OK rows |r|>0.5: 4' / E3-AC4 PASS. M2 PLANTED: 'gold rows at 2026-09-25: 959 | missing 1' / E3-AC1 FAIL. M2 RESTORED: 'gold rows at 2026-09-25: 960 | missing 0' / E3-AC1 PASS. Both criteria are live oracles and neither passes on absence.
mutant.note: M2 also shows the limit of the manifest half of E3-AC1 in isolation: with the row dropped straight out of the parquet, the manifest still read accounts_with_prior_holdings 960 / complete true, because the manifest was computed by the producer from the frame it emitted and not from the bytes that survived. The criterion catches it anyway -- the row-level 'missing 1' limb fires -- but a manifest is a producer's SELF-REPORT and the row count is the independent instrument. Worth stating rather than leaving for someone to discover.

determinism.method: Three instruments on the same population. (a) The date=2026-09-25 partition of EACH channel was produced three times -- the pre-run dry run, the full-range upload, and the mutant restore -- and the census compared across all three. (b) The landed row totals were read back from the parquet FOOTERS (an instrument the producer does not touch) and compared with the producer's own printed tally. (c) The 24-test suite was re-run against the final committed bytes.
